entry: Numeral system using ten as its base (radix). Its most common form is the [[Hindu–Arabic numeral system]], a positional system with ten digits, 0 to 9, which made very large numbers far easier to write and calculate with and was later extended to represent decimal fractions. A decimal separator, usually "." in English-speaking countries and "," in many others, marks the fractional part, as in 25.9703 or 3.1415. Non-positional base-ten systems include [[Roman numerals]] and Chinese numerals. Many ancient civilizations used ten and its powers, possibly because people counted on their fingers. A decimal fraction is a number of the form a/10ⁿ, where a is an integer and n is a non-negative integer. An infinite decimal represents a [[Rational number|rational number]] if and only if it repeats or has finitely many nonzero digits.

headword: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
sort_key: declaration of the rights of man and of the citizen
entry: Human and civil rights document of the [[French Revolution]]. Its last article was adopted by the National Constituent Assembly on August 26, 1789, as the first step toward a constitution for the Kingdom of France. [[Marquis de Lafayette]] prepared the initial drafts with assistance from [[Thomas Jefferson]], but most of the final text came from Abbé Sieyès. Drawing on Enlightenment thinkers such as [[Montesquieu]] and [[Jean-Jacques Rousseau]], it declares that "men are born and remain free and equal in rights" and treats liberty, property, security and resistance to oppression as natural rights. Its principles excluded women, slaves and non-property owners from full citizenship. The declaration was placed at the beginning of the constitutions of the French Fourth Republic (1946) and Fifth Republic (1958).

Process by which dead organic matter is broken down into simpler organic or inorganic substances, such as [[Carbon dioxide|carbon dioxide]], water, simple sugars and mineral salts. It is part of the nutrient cycle and recycles finite matter within the [[Biosphere]]. Abiotic decomposition involves chemical or physical processes such as hydrolysis, while biotic decomposition, or biodegradation, is the metabolic breakdown of materials by living organisms, typically [[Microorganism|microorganisms]]. Decomposers, or detritivores, include bacteria, fungi and animals such as [[Earthworm|earthworms]]. In animals, decay begins at death through autolysis, the breakdown of tissues by the body's own enzymes, and putrefaction by bacteria, which releases cadaverine and putrescine, the chief source of the [[Odor|odor]] of decaying tissue. Rates depend on temperature, moisture, oxygen and soil pH.

Arts of designing and making objects that are both beautiful and functional. The field covers most objects used to furnish building interiors, along with interior design, but typically excludes [[Architecture]]. Major groupings include [[Ceramic art|ceramics]], metalwork, [[Furniture]], [[Jewellery]], fashion, textile arts and glassware. Decorative arts are often contrasted with the fine arts of [[Painting]], drawing, photography and large-scale [[Sculpture]], which produce objects solely for their aesthetic quality. The distinction is much less meaningful for [[Islamic art]] and [[Chinese art]], where many valued works were decorative. In the 1970s, writers including Amy Goldin and Anne Swartz formally challenged the view of decoration as a lesser art. Applied arts largely overlap with decorative arts, and both are now often placed under the umbrella of design.

Form of reasoning in which a conclusion follows logically from its premises. An inference is valid if the premises cannot be true while the conclusion is false, and an argument is sound if it is valid and all its premises are true. A classic example infers "Socrates is mortal" from the premises "all men are mortal" and "Socrates is a man." Deductive logic studies when an argument is valid, using rules of inference such as modus ponens and modus tollens; invalid deductive arguments are called formal fallacies. Unlike [[Inductive reasoning|inductive]] reasoning, deduction gives certainty within its premises but adds no information beyond them. Research in the [[Psychology|psychology]] of reasoning finds that people draw valid inferences more successfully from modus ponens than from modus tollens, and that concrete cases are easier than abstract ones. Natural deduction is a proof system built on self-evident rules of inference.

British rock band formed in 1968. Considered among the pioneers of heavy metal and hard rock, the band moved from psychedelic and progressive rock to a heavier sound with *Deep Purple in Rock* (1970). It is referred to as part of the "unholy trinity" of British hard rock with [[Led Zeppelin]] and [[Black Sabbath]]. Listed in the 1975 Guinness Book of World Records as "the globe's loudest band," it has sold over 100 million records and was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2016.

Cultural and geographic subregion of the Southern United States. The term generally denotes Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia and South Carolina, the states most economically dependent on plantation agriculture and slavery. During Reconstruction, emancipated people asserted their rights, which incited the growth of the Ku Klux Klan. After the federal government withdrew following the Compromise of 1877, Jim Crow laws suppressed African Americans' civil rights for almost a century, until the civil rights movement of the 1950s and 1960s. The region is part of the [[Bible Belt]] and a stronghold of the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]].

1972 American pornographic film written and directed by Gerard Damiano. It starred [[Linda Lovelace]] and is considered the forefront of the Golden Age of Porn (1969–1984). One of the first pornographic films with a plot, character development and relatively high production values, it earned mainstream attention and launched the "porno chic" trend, although it was the subject of obscenity trials and banned in some jurisdictions. Lovelace later claimed that she was coerced and sexually assaulted during production.

Branch of [[Machine learning|machine learning]] that uses multilayered [[Neural network (machine learning)|neural networks]]. The "deep" refers to the use of multiple layers, ranging from three to several hundred or thousands, through which data are transformed into increasingly abstract representations. Common architectures include convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks and transformers. Applied to computer vision, speech recognition, natural language processing and drug design, deep learning has produced results comparable to, and sometimes surpassing, human expert performance. Current networks are not intended to model the functioning of the [[Human brain|human brain]].

Fish inhabiting the dark ocean below the sunlit surface waters. The lanternfish is by far the most common, and others include the flashlight fish, cookiecutter shark, bristlemouths, [[Anglerfish|anglerfish]] and viperfish. The deep sea makes up about 90% of ocean volume and is in darkness, with temperatures that rarely exceed 3 °C and pressures between 20 and 1,000 atm. Adaptations include bioluminescent organs for predation, counter-illumination [[Camouflage|camouflage]], enlarged hinged jaws and stomachs that allow prolonged fasting. The earliest known records of deep-sea fish are trace fossils of feeding and swimming behavior from the 130-million-year-old Early Cretaceous Palombini Shale of [[Italy]].

Parts of the [[World Wide Web]] whose contents are not indexed by standard [[Search engine|search engines]]. Computer scientist Michael K. Bergman is credited with inventing the term in 2001. The deep web includes web mail, online banking, cloud storage, restricted social-media pages, forums that require registration, and paywalled services such as video on demand. Many media outlets have used "deep web" synonymously with the [[Dark web|dark web]], a usage some reject; the dark web is the part of the deep web hidden intentionally and inaccessible to standard browsers. Estimates put the deep web at about 90% or more of the internet's content volume.

Indian actress known mainly for Hindi-language films. One of India's highest-paid actresses, she has won three Filmfare Awards and was named one of the 100 most influential people in the world by [[Time (magazine)|Time]] in 2018. She made her Bollywood debut opposite [[Shah Rukh Khan]] in *Om Shanti Om* (2007) and later won two Filmfare Awards for Best Actress, for *Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela* and *Piku*. She founded The Live Love Laugh Foundation, which works to raise awareness of mental health in India.

Hoofed [[Ruminant|ruminant]] ungulate of the family Cervidae. Male deer of almost all species, except the water deer, and female [[Reindeer]] grow and shed bony antlers each year, which are often used in combat between males. The family divides into the subfamilies Cervinae, including muntjac, elk, red deer and fallow deer, and Capreolinae, including reindeer, white-tailed deer, roe deer and [[Moose]]. Deer appear in art from Paleolithic cave paintings onward and have figured in mythology, religion, literature and [[Heraldry]]. Their meat is eaten as venison, their skins make soft buckskin, and their antlers serve as knife handles. Deer live in biomes from tundra to tropical rainforest and are indigenous to every continent except Antarctica and Australia.

English rock band formed in [[Sheffield]]. It was part of the new wave of British heavy metal in the early 1980s. Its album *Hysteria* (1987) topped the UK, US, Canadian and Australian charts and has sold over 15 million copies worldwide. The earlier album *Pyromania* (1983) was certified Diamond in the United States. The band has sold more than 100 million records and was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2019.

Biological process by which organisms eliminate solid, semisolid or liquid waste, known as [[Feces|feces]], from the digestive tract through the [[Anus|anus]] or [[Cloaca|cloaca]]. It follows digestion, and waves of muscular contraction called peristalsis move waste through the colon toward the rectum. Humans defecate from a few times daily to a few times weekly. In infants, defecation occurs by reflex, while in adults the external anal sphincter is under voluntary control, learned through toilet training. Conditions such as [[Diarrhea|diarrhea]] and constipation are associated with it, and feces can spread disease, most often through contaminated food. Open defecation, the practice of defecating outside without any toilet, remains widespread in some developing countries, while well-developed countries use [[Sewage treatment|sewage treatment]] plants.

Fortification built to protect a city, town or other settlement from attackers. Walls range from palisades and earthworks to extensive curtain walls with towers, bastions and gates. Some, such as the [[Great Wall of China]] and [[Hadrian's Wall]], extended far beyond city borders to enclose regions or mark territorial boundaries. Most surviving ancient walls are [[Masonry|masonry]] structures. [[Uruk]] in [[Sumer]] is among the world's oldest known walled cities, and the proto-city of Jericho had a wall by the 8th millennium BC. [[Babylon]] was expanded by Nebuchadnezzar, who also built its Ishtar Gate, and the Assyrians deployed large labor forces to build defensive walls. Gunpowder artillery later rendered high, thin walls vulnerable, and the Theodosian Walls of [[Constantinople]] were breached by Ottoman cannons in 1453.

Decline in the general price level of goods and services, measured by broad price indices. Deflation is a monetary phenomenon, explained by changes in the money supply and velocity relative to spending on output. It is distinct from [[Inflation|disinflation]], a slowdown in inflation that remains positive. Because deflation increases the real value of [[Debt|debt]], a large unexpected deflationary shock is generally considered a problem in a modern economy. When prices are falling, consumers may delay purchases, which idles productive capacity and reduces investment in a deflationary spiral. Deflation also results when rising productivity lowers prices. Some analyses of 17 countries from 1870 to 1999 find no strong causal link between deflation and depressions, while during the [[Great Depression]] prices in the United States fell by about 25%.

Removal and destruction of forest for conversion to non-forest use, such as farms, ranches or urban development. Forests cover about 31% of Earth's land surface, one-third less than before the expansion of [[Agriculture|agriculture]]. Agriculture directly causes nearly 90% of global deforestation as of 2025, mainly through cropland expansion and pasture creation, and plantations of coffee, palm oil and rubber also drive clearing. Livestock grazing, logging, urbanization, mining and [[Wildfire|wildfires]] contribute. Deforestation causes habitat destruction and [[Biodiversity|biodiversity]] loss, extinction, and displacement of indigenous people, and it reduces the uptake of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Since 1990, about 420 million hectares of forest have been lost, although the estimated rate fell from 16 million hectares per year in the 1990s to 10 million hectares per year in 2015–2020.

Clearing of tree cover across the [[Amazon rainforest]], largely for cattle ranching and [[Soybean|soybean]] farming. The Amazon covers about 3,000,000 sq km, and Brazil contains about 60% of it. Cattle ranching is identified as the primary cause of deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon, accounting for about 80% of clearing in the region. Soybean expansion also destroys forest directly as "soy frontiers" advance. Satellite data from 2018 revealed a decade-high rate, with about 7,900 sq km destroyed between August 2017 and July 2018.

Change in the size or shape of an object when subjected to [[Force|force]]. Deformation is elastic if the object returns to its original shape when the force is removed, and plastic if permanent distortion remains. An object's resistance to deformation is its [[Stiffness|stiffness]] or rigidity. Within the elastic range, stress and strain are generally linear, and the linear relationship for a material is known as [[Young's modulus]]. Small-strain theory suits materials such as [[Steel|steel]] and [[Concrete|concrete]], which deform only slightly under engineering loads. Elastomers, rubber and some shape-memory metals such as Nitinol show large elastic deformation, but their elasticity is nonlinear, so other strain definitions are needed.

Dense state of matter at low temperature, in which the [[Pauli exclusion principle]] significantly alters behavior. In [[Astrophysics|astrophysics]], the term refers to dense stellar remnants such as [[White dwarf|white dwarfs]] and [[Neutron star|neutron stars]], whose thermal pressure alone cannot prevent gravitational collapse. It is usually modeled as an ideal Fermi gas of non-interacting [[Fermion|fermions]] that fill the lowest quantum states. This degeneracy pressure remains nonzero even at [[Absolute zero]] and depends on the density of the fermions rather than on temperature, which keeps dense stars in equilibrium. The term also applies to metals in the Fermi gas approximation. The concept of degenerate stars was developed jointly by Arthur Eddington, Ralph Fowler and Arthur Milne.

Unit of plane angle in which one full rotation equals 360 degrees, usually denoted by °. The [[International System of Units|SI]] unit of angular measure is the [[Radian|radian]], and one degree equals π/180 radians. Theories link the choice of 360 to the approximately 360 days of the year and to Babylonian sexagesimal numbers. [[Hipparchus]] and [[Archimedes]] were among the first Greeks known to divide the circle into 360 degrees of 60 arcminutes each. The number's divisibility also suits the division of the world into 24 [[Time zone|time zones]] of 15° of longitude each. Subdivisions include the arcminute (1/60 of a degree) and the arcsecond; maritime charts use decimal minutes, where one minute of [[Latitude|latitude]] equals one nautical mile.

Smaller and outer of the two natural satellites of [[Mars]], the other being [[Phobos (moon)|Phobos]]. It has a mean radius of 6.2 km and takes 30.3 hours to orbit Mars at a distance of 23,457.50 km. It is named after the Greek personification of dread and terror. Asaph Hall discovered it at the United States Naval Observatory on August 12, 1877. Its origin is unresolved: it may have been captured from the [[Asteroid belt]], or a 2021 proposal holds that it formed from a common parent body with Phobos that broke apart 1 to 2.7 billion years ago.

[[American football]] coach and former player, nicknamed "Prime Time." He played 14 seasons in the [[National Football League]] and nine in [[Major League Baseball]], winning two [[Super Bowl]] titles. He made one [[World Series]] appearance, in 1992, and is the only athlete in history to have played in both a Super Bowl and a World Series. Selected fifth overall in the 1989 NFL draft, he was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2011. He later served as head coach at Jackson State University from 2020 to 2022 and at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Belief in a creator God who does not intervene in the universe after creating it. Deists hold that reason and observation of the natural world are sufficient to establish God's existence, and they reject prophecies, revelations and religious texts as reliable sources of divine knowledge. Deism rests on natural theology, in which God's existence is revealed through nature itself. Deistic thinking has ancient roots, but Deists emerged in the 17th century and during the [[Age of Enlightenment]], especially in England, France and North America. Figures including [[Voltaire]] and [[Thomas Paine]] criticized organized religion from this position. Deistic ideas were later absorbed into movements such as [[Unitarianism]].
